title: Directionality of title element

labels.name: i18n-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of Internationalization, or tracked by i18n but not needing response.

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
In the section of [the title element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-title-element), the last paragraph says:
> User agents should use the document's title when referring to the document in their user interface. When the contents of a `title` element are used in this way, the directionality of that `title` element should be used to set the directionality of the document's title in the user interface.

This doesn't match what browsers currently do, and it doesn't work as expected for many RTL pages.

Chrome and Safari currently solely rely on the first strong character in the title. Firefox always uses the UI locale direction which makes no sense.

On the other hand, many pages written in RTL scripts don't have `dir="rtl"` specified in their document level, and consequently `title` element would inherit ltr. (I opened Hebrew wikipedia, and randomly pick some reference pages from its articles. I checked 6 Hebrew sites from there, and only 2 of them have `dir="rtl"` in their `html` tag. Other sites just apply the direction to its content.)

I think that we should setup some special rule for directionality of `title` element given these.

I think there are several options:
1. make directionality of `title` element solely depend on the first strong character like what some browsers currently do, or
2. use the first strong character when the `dir` attribute of both `title` element and all its ancestors are in the `auto` state.

The second option might have more desirable result, but it may be harder to implement, because browsers would need to store directionality of `title` element in addition to its content. That's probably not a big deal, I guess.

WDYT?
